documents.abstract: The increasing demand for renewable energy and the urgent need to mitigate climate change have driven global interest in bioethanol as a sustainable alternative to fossil fuels. However, reliance on edible feedstocks such as corn, sugarcane or wheat has proven unsustainable due to food-fuel competition. In contrast, second-generation bioethanol production that utilizes lignocellulosic biomass primarily depends on a single biomass, limiting the continuous production because of seasonal variability and high production costs. Mixed lignocellulosic biomass (MLB) utilization has emerged as a promising strategy to address these challenges by integrating diverse agricultural residues, forestry waste, energy crops and industrial by-products within biorefineries. MLB provides supply stability, enhances enzymatic saccharification and minimizes inhibitor formation through synergistic buffering and compositional complementarity. This review comprehensively evaluates the significance of feedstock diversity, pretreatment strategies, enzymatic hydrolysis and fermentation approaches in MLB-based bioethanol production. It further examines process integration strategies, such as simultaneous saccharification and fermentation, consolidated bioprocessing and hybrid reactor systems for year-round operations. Techno-economic assessments demonstrate that MLB reduces the production costs, while life-cycle analyses confirm significant greenhouse gas mitigation potential. Despite these advantages, this study describes challenges in feedstock logistics, inhibitor management, strain robustness and process stability. Moreover, it outlines future directions that emphasize the roles of artificial intelligence and machine learning in feedstock blending, synthetic biology for robust microbial consortia and supportive policy frameworks to promote biomass aggregation. Overall, MLB represents a scalable and sustainable pathway for continuous second-generation bioethanol production, offering environmental, economic and technological advantages over single-feed approaches.

AI agents are increasingly expected to modify and maintain machine-learning systems in production, yet existing benchmarks primarily evaluate either competition-style ML experimentation or generic repository issue resolution. We introduce MLOps-Bench, a repository-grounded benchmark for production ML engineering. Unlike prior ML-agent benchmarks, MLOps-Bench evaluates executable lifecycle changes inside real ML repositories, spanning data pipelines, feature engineering, model training, model serving, monitoring, CI/CD and governance, and end-to-end integration. Each task is grounded in repository evidence and includes a natural-language requirement, oracle patch, plausible buggy baseline, fail-to-pass tests, pass-to-pass tests, and provenance metadata. The benchmark contains 212 validated tasks from 31 public ML repositories, with 636 fail-to-pass tests and 856 pass-to-pass tests. We evaluate six agents and find that the best system solves 31.2% of tasks while passing 68.7% of tests, showing that current agents often make partial progress but still fail production-relevant behavioral requirements. MLOps-Bench shifts agent evaluation beyond model building and issue fixing toward repository-native MLOps work where correctness depends on lifecycle reasoning, behavioral robustness, and preservation of existing system behavior.

Multimodal large language model (MLLM)-based mobile agents are rapidly evolving from conversational assistants into autonomous systems that perceive, reason over, and act on smartphone environments. This capability also exposes a new security risk: adversaries can embed malicious objectives in cross-application mobile content and steer agent behavior through indirect multimodal injection. Although prompt injection has been studied in desktop and web settings, its cross-modal properties in mobile ecosystems remain poorly understood, and existing security analyses are still limited. To close this gap, we introduce MobileInject, the first benchmark for evaluating mobile agents against multimodal injection attacks and reasoning-to-action security risks. MobileInject provides a high-fidelity interactive mobile evaluation framework covering 11 scenarios, 9 security-risk categories, and 108 executable risk instances. It further introduces Cross-Modal Consistency Injection to exploit corroboration across modalities, two enhanced attack methods, Multi-Role Collaborative Deception and Reasoning-Camouflage Injection, to intensify trust manipulation and reasoning hijacking, and a Reasoning Security Diagnosis Framework for fine-grained failure analysis. Systematic experiments show that mobile agents are broadly vulnerable to multimodal injection, and that many failures stem from reasoning hijacking at early stages. These findings establish MobileInject as a systematic cross-modal benchmark for studying and improving the security of mobile agents. Code release details are provided in the Appendix Open Science section.

Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly incorporated into agent-based models (ABMs) on the premise that richer, context-sensitive human behavior can improve empirical fidelity. However, LLM-supported ABMs introduce an open-ended design space in which subtle modeling and configuration choices, such as prompt design and environment coupling, can substantially alter outcomes. Developing LLM-supported ABMs to simulate human collective behavior therefore requires navigating configuration sensitivity while identifying the limitations of the current model architecture. In this paper, we introduce the \textit{Model Capacity Frontier} (MCF), a framework that characterizes the empirical performance attainable by a specified architecture across its admissible configurations. In multi-objective settings, this capacity is represented by an estimated Pareto frontier obtained through systematic configuration exploration. We demonstrate MCF in crowd simulation of university commencement events with approximately 12,000 agents, using empirical movement data on temporal occupancy, spatial distribution, and flow direction. We first characterize the capacity of a conventional crowd model and then evaluate successive LLM-supported architectural extensions. In the process, MCF reveals which dimensions of attainable performance expand and which remain limited, providing empirical targets for refinement and re-evaluation. Initial LLM integration improves flow direction but degrades temporal occupancy and spatial distribution; subsequent architectural refinement of the LLM layer improves temporal occupancy and recovers spatial performance, while retaining much of the earlier gain in flow direction. Our case study shows how MCF guides the systematic architectural development of LLM-supported ABMs in configuration-sensitive, open-ended design spaces.

Historical pre-crash scenarios contain a sequence of vehicle-to-vehicle interactions, among which the critical pre-crash interaction is the one that most directly leads to the eventual collision. Identifying such critical interactions is important for uncovering potential safety risks in Autonomous Driving Systems (ADSs). However, this task remains challenging because the critical interaction is often embedded within numerous preceding interactions and needs to be distinguished by considering how the pre-crash scenario evolves over time. To address this challenge, we propose MICA, a model-based multi-agent approach for identifying critical pre-crash interactions from textual accident reports. Unlike existing LLM-based approaches that directly identify critical interactions from accident reports, MICA explicitly models the evolution of pre-crash interactions through multi-agent collaboration. Specialized LLM-based agents extract and validate relevant information to construct a Pre-crash Evolution Model, from which the critical interaction is identified by matching the modeled interactions to predefined pre-crash patterns. We evaluate MICA on 200 accident reports released by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and the California Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV CA). The results demonstrate that MICA effectively identifies critical pre-crash interactions across different accident report data sources, scenario complexities, and underlying LLMs.

The objective of this study was to use artificial intelligence (AI) to predict mastery-approach goals in secondary school students based on variables from the PISA 2018 database. The sample consisted of 339,560 participants from 60 countries. Machine learning was used with the Super Learner mega-algorithm with 14 candidate algorithms. In addition, deep learning was used with a neural network with 107 parameters. The analyses showed that students’ perceived parental emotional support, competitiveness, purpose in life, self-efficacy, and knowledge of intercultural communication were predictors of mastery-approach goals in secondary school students. This research contributes to the study of factors that influence mastery-approach goals in secondary school students, with analysis models that advance the development of the science of AI-based predictive education.

Modern LLM applications rely on runtime monitors that inspect tool calls, traces, streams, detector outputs, and verifier inputs. This creates an interface-reliability problem: a framework path may remain operational while policy-relevant evidence never reaches its decision point. In one representative case, a regex detector returned a positive match, but the framework stranded the result before the block decision. This differs from jailbreaks and detector errors because the evidence is already recognized yet disconnected from enforcement. We study this repair-boundary signature with canary contracts: parent/fixed confirmation units that place a known payload only on the changed evidence surface and record monitor visibility together with the downstream decision for action-boundary cases. Applying the protocol to public framework repairs, we confirm 18 evidence-path failures across 11 LLM or agent safety project groups and four implementation ecosystems. Nine are established-boundary repairs, eight are new-surface policy-coverage gaps, and one is a boundary-only evidence case. Fourteen reach E1 enforcement boundaries: seven native action outcomes, six configured enforcement boundaries, and one synthetic-consumer consequence. The remaining cases affect verifier, safety-prompt, or observability channels. The cases form carrier, adapter, authority, and surface families and show how ordinary application behavior can remain intact while a safety-specific evidence path misses its decision. Exact revisions, deterministic outcomes, negative controls, and a frozen prospective audit document the confirmation rule. Monitor assumptions therefore need regression tests at the schemas, streams, tools, and adapters that frameworks evolve.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Multi-turn image editing aims to modify an image according to a sequence of instructions, making it better aligned with human-AI collaborative creation than single-turn editing. However, constructing high-quality multi-turn training data remains challenging, as conventional sequential rollout accumulates errors and introduces visual-quality drift across editing turns. To address this challenge, we introduce MTEdit, a multi-turn image editing dataset built through a pipeline centered on packed trajectory canvas (PTC) generation. By jointly generating multiple editing states within a unified visual context, this pipeline reduces visual-quality drift across turns. Covering both step-wise and context-aware editing scenarios, MTEdit comprises 500K multi-turn image editing trajectories, with up to 8 turns and an average of 5.38 turns per trajectory, making it one of the most extensive datasets for multi-turn image editing. We further introduce MTEdit-Bench, a benchmark designed to evaluate both scenarios by assessing models' ability to follow editing instructions, maintain content consistency, resist visual-quality drift, and effectively use historical context across turns. Using MTEdit, we fine-tune Qwen-Image-Edit-Causal to obtain Qwen-Image-MTEdit. On MTEdit-Bench, we evaluate a broad range of closed-source and open-source image editing models, including Qwen-Image-MTEdit. Experimental results show that Qwen-Image-MTEdit achieves the best performance among the evaluated open-source models, demonstrating the effectiveness of MTEdit in improving models' multi-turn image editing capabilities.
topics: Generative Adversarial Networks and Image Synthesis

documents.abstract: We investigate the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) in multi-author style change detection. Using off-the-shelf LLMs or supervised fine-tuning solely within the target domain fails to yield effective features; for this reason, we propose cross-domain transfer learning with LLM-based embeddings fine-tuned for authorship verification. We fine-tune Mistral-7B embedding model and compare it with DeBERTa, used in the state-of-the-art (SOTA) systems in PAN-25 multi-author writing style analysis challenge. Results show that DeBERTa and Mistral excel in different user-generated text scenarios. We exploit this diversity by combining both embeddings, leading to more effective style change detection.

The construction industry faces growing challenges that require better decision-making frameworks. Combining Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) with digital tools like Building Information Modeling (BIM) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) offers a promising way forward. Yet their integration remains fragmented across research efforts, revealing a significant gap in theory and practice. As a result, their potential remains underutilized, limiting the development of flexible, data-driven decision-making tools for complex construction projects. This study conducts a systematic bibliometric analysis to map the development and structure of the MCDM-BIM-AI connection in construction management from 2015 to 2025. Using a PRISMA-compliant protocol, we analyzed 253 peer-reviewed articles from the Scopus database. Our approach combines performance analysis with science mapping through keyword co-occurrence networks and thematic evolution analysis across three time periods: 2015-2018, 2019-2021, 2022-2025, along with a country-level co-authorship network analysis. Our findings identify five main thematic clusters and show a significant increase in publications since 2019, mainly driven by the Asia-Pacific region. The analysis highlights a notable knowledge gap in the deep connection between BIM and AI within MCDM frameworks. The temporal mapping reveals three phases of evolution: pre-integration (2015-2018), Integration (2019-2021), and Innovation (2022-present), with AI and Machine Learning becoming key focus areas in the latest phase. The study suggests promising future directions for combining MCDM, BIM, and AI to promote more sustainable, data-driven, and resilient construction practices. It proposes a conceptual outline for the Intelligent Cognitive Decision Framework (ICDF), where BIM serves as a semantic data backbone, MCDM acts as the evaluation engine, and AI provides cognitive support for flexible, data-driven decision-making in construction 4.0 applications. This intellectual mapping offers researchers data-driven guidance for prioritizing impactful investigations, practitioners with technology investment plans that match research developments, and policymakers with informed priorities for research and development investment in underrepresented regions.

In a hierarchical multi-agent system, a Leader assigns tasks and subagents carry them out. Jointly training the Leader and the subagents is difficult because a final answer gives only indirect feedback to the subagents. An LLM judge can score the performance of the subagents, but these scores depend on the judge's own assessment of the quality of subagents' responses. We present MultiAgent-OPD, which combines on-policy distillation with reinforcement learning to jointly train a shared-parameter Leader-Searcher-Answerer team end to end. We first train a Teacher in a Searcher-Answerer workflow using answer correctness. During team training, the frozen Teacher scores student-generated search and summary tokens to provide local process supervision for the Searchers, while the Leader learns from team success and the Answerer from candidate correctness. Across seven datasets, the trained system reaches 38.68% macro avg@4, exceeding Prompted Critic by 4.06 percentage points and C-MAS + RL, the trained cascaded multiagent system, by 2.61 percentage points. The team also solves more questions within four attempts.

The reuse of open government works on the web has increased rapidly with the expansion of public data policies and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted content utilization. In Korea, Korea Open Government Licenses (KOGLs) permit the reuse of public works under conditions such as attribution, non-commercial use, and no-derivatives. However, these conditions are frequently violated or misunderstood in web pages, advertisements, social media posts, and reused digital content. Since compliance-related evidence is distributed across textual descriptions, captions, license metadata, embedded image text, visual changes, and page-level context, manual inspection, and single-modal analysis are not sufficient for scalable web-based compliance review. This paper proposes a multimodal evidence-based method for KOGL license compliance risk prediction in web environments. The proposed method combines textual context, KOGL metadata, optical character recognition (OCR) extracted image text, and visual features to classify four risk types: attribution risk, non-commercial use risk, no-derivatives risk, and false KOGL claim risk. A lightweight sequential context model captures the contextual flow of compliance-related cues, while the decision module produces both risk probabilities and evidence-based explanations. Experiments on a KOGL-oriented dataset show that the proposed method achieves higher accuracy, macro-F1, and area under the curve (AUC) than text-only, image-only, and simple fusion baselines. The results demonstrate that multimodal web evidence improves compliance risk prediction and provides practical support for human review in public content management, open government data curation, and AI training data inspection.

Multi-turn jailbreaks use feedback from a victim large language model to adapt their queries over several turns. However, once an effective trajectory has been found, it is unclear how much of the earlier query history is still needed. In this work, we study this by removing early attacker queries and running the remaining queries again in a new conversation while regenerating the victim's responses. We define the effective horizon as the shortest remaining query sequence that recovers the same attack progress. Empirically, we find that roughly half of the original query sequence is sufficient on average to recover the same attack progress. We call this phenomenon effective-horizon compression. We show that this shorter history can recover the best point reached during an unsuccessful attack and provide a better starting point for continuing the attack. It also helps identify which earlier queries should receive less learning signal during attacker training, and downweighting those queries improves performance. We further find that short reward-propagation windows preserve calibrated defense performance close to full-trajectory returns. These results show that multi-turn attacks can contain more queries than are needed to recover the progress reached later in the interaction.

This study aimed to assess musculoskeletal and ergonomic risk, identify demographic, occupational, lifestyle, and biomechanical characteristics associated with these outcomes, and develop and prioritize ergonomic intervention strategies for petrochemical control room operators. This cross-sectional study was conducted in 2025 among 210 male control room operators from an Iranian petrochemical complex using census sampling. Data were collected using the Demographic/Occupational Questionnaire, Persian International Physical Activity Questionnaire (P-IPAQ), Persian Örebro Musculoskeletal Pain Screening Questionnaire (P-ÖMSQ), and Persian Ergonomic Screening and Priority Tool (P-ESPT), complemented by objective postural and plantar pressure assessments. The P-ÖMSQ was used to classify participants according to P-ÖMSQ risk categories, with scores ≥ 90 categorized as moderate-to-high risk. Data were analyzed using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) software, version 20.0, with descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and multivariable logistic regression. A P-ÖMSQ score within the moderate-to-high risk categories (≥ 90) was observed in 27% of participants, while 78% were classified as having moderate-to-high ergonomic risk. Multivariable logistic regression showed that older age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 1.09, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.02–1.17, p = 0.014), higher body mass index (BMI) (aOR = 1.15, 95% CI = 1.04–1.27, p = 0.006), and longer job tenure (aOR = 1.98, 95% CI = 1.01–3.89, p = 0.047) were independently associated with higher odds of being classified in the moderate-to-high-risk P-ÖMSQ category. Lower physical activity was significantly associated with a higher prevalence of forward head posture, thoracic hyperkyphosis, lateral pelvic tilt, and pes planus ( p < 0.05). Objective biomechanical abnormalities were also significantly associated with higher P-ÖMSQ-based and P-ESPT-based risk categories ( p < 0.05). Based on the study findings, 20 ergonomic intervention strategies were proposed and prioritized through a stakeholder-informed participatory process. Older age, higher body mass index, and longer job tenure were associated with higher odds of being classified in the moderate-to-high-risk P-ÖMSQ category, while lower physical activity was associated with selected postural abnormalities among petrochemical control room operators. Several objective biomechanical abnormalities were also associated with P-ÖMSQ-based and P-ESPT-based risk categories. These findings may inform the prioritization of workplace ergonomic interventions; however, the proposed interventions were not evaluated in the present study, and their effectiveness should be assessed in future longitudinal and interventional studies.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Colleges record semester results in spreadsheets, and answering even a simple question about them, such as how one section performed compared with another, usually means filtering and calculating by hand or writing SQL. This paper presents the Natural Language Database Query and Analytics Agent, a system that lets non-technical users ask such questions in plain English. The agent supplies the schema of a relational database to a large language model, which writes a SQL query. The query is checked, executed in read-only mode, corrected using the database error message if it fails, and the result is returned as text, a table or a chart. The design is applied to the Information Science and Engineering result sheets of 206 students over three semesters (IV, V and VI). Example questions are run against the prepared database, and their answers are reported as ground truth for future testing, along with data-quality problems found in the source sheets. The measured accuracy of the model-generated queries is left for future work.

By automating the content creation process, Generative AI is reshaping creative work, but its impact on knowledge workers remains underexplored, which this study seeks to examine. Drawing on in-depth interviews with 20 knowledge workers, this study examines what is being transformed in the workplace and how these shifts are being perceived by the knowledge workers who use GenAI. Using Social Shaping of Technology (SST) as a conceptual lens to understand the interaction between technology and knowledge workers, the study finds that participants perceived GenAI as an efficient tool that provides cognitive relief and enhances productivity during times of resource constraint. Tensions also arose around authenticity, creativity, a sense of fulfillment, and the perception of effort. The adoption of GenAI has created downstream labor and demand for new skills as it shifts knowledge workers’ roles away from creator to editor/fact-checker while creating tension as participants balance their desire for efficiency with fears of diminished creativity and domain knowledge, skills atrophy, and threats to content ownership.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: This chapter addresses the rapid integration of AI technology, especially Gen AI, into our lives and especially the teaching and learning practices in higher education, foregrounding a range of unresolved social, ecological and academic issues this entails. A ninth capability is proposed as necessary for flourishing in this complex technology-infused age. The chapter also discusses the linkages between inquiry, integrity, learning, and Artificial Intelligence.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: IoT botnets generate diverse network behaviors, including scanning, command-and-control communication, and distributed denial-of-service activity. Traditional machine learn-ing models can achieve high detection accuracy using engineered network-flow features, but they often provide limited behav-ioral explanation. This work presents a network flow-window framework for IoT botnet behavior detection and explanation using both conventional machine learning baselines and a multi-agent large language model (LLM) reasoning pipeline. The proposed approach aggregates Zeek network flows into fixed-size behavioral windows and uses two IoT-23 scenarios: a scanning-dominated scenario for behavior-window construction and a main three-class scenario containing benign, C&C, and DDoS behavior. For the second scenario, non-leakage machine learning baselines achieved strong performance, with XGBoost and Random Forest reaching 99.42% accuracy using only network-derived window features. The multi-agent LLM pipeline, consisting of a behavior analyst, threat classifier, and judge agent, achieved 98.24% classifier accuracy and 97.65% judge accuracy over valid parsed outputs on a balanced 342-window evaluation set. When one invalid JSON response is counted as an automated failure, the end-to-end judge accuracy is 97.37%. Error analysis showed that most remaining errors occurred in behaviorally ambiguous cases, particularly benign windows with high-volume one-way DNS-like traffic and low-volume C&C windows mixed with benign-looking NTP traffic. The results suggest that conventional ML remains highly effective for structured classification, while multi-agent LLM reasoning adds interpretable evidence-based analysis and supports more transparent investigation of IoT botnet behavior.
topics: Internet Traffic Analysis and Secure E-voting

documents.abstract: Relevance. Medical device safety monitoring is one of the consistently and strictly controlled mandatory requirements imposed on healthcare organizations. Objective: to analyze the new Procedure for the implementation of medical device safety monitoring and the new Procedure for reporting adverse events in the field of medical device circulation with a view to identifying the new tasks now facing healthcare organizations. Results. It is noted that the new orders of the Ministry of Health of the Russian Federation have significantly clarified and detailed the requirements for information, the collection, processing, and recording of which are carried out during medical device safety monitoring. This includes, inter alia, data transmitted by software employing artificial intelligence technologies that constitutes a medical device; information on adverse events in the field of medical device circulation in other states; and information contained in an adverse event report. Attention is drawn to the increased significance of the Classification of adverse events related to the circulation of medical devices. Conclusion. Healthcare organizations should pay special attention to the fact that the identification of adverse events in the field of medical device circulation must now be carried out in strict accordance with the Classification of adverse events approved by Order No. 4513 of the Federal Service for Surveillance in Healthcare (Roszdravnadzor) dated May 20, 2021. In accordance with the new Procedure for the implementation of medical device safety monitoring, each healthcare organization is required to appoint an official responsible for organizing the work of collecting information in order to ensure the safe use of medical devices and to establish the procedure for this work.

topics: Generative Adversarial Networks and Image Synthesis

documents.abstract: Bridging the gap between human intent and machine logic remains a critical challenge in data access for non-technical users, yet Large Language Models (LLMs) remain unreliable: they hallucinate schema elements, generate syntactically invalid queries, or fail to capture user intent. These limitations are especially critical in domains such as insurance, where KPIs, regulatory constraints, and legacy relational systems demand high precision. We introduce a multi-agent, persona-driven NL2SQL framework that combines (1) domain relevance detection, (2) schema-grounded knowledge construction, (3) KPI-aware SQL synthesis, (4) syntax-level self-repair using sqlite execution feedback, and (5) semantic consistency checking via SQL-to-NL reverse engineering. Our system significantly reduces query hallucination and improves semantic fidelity compared to direct LLM prompting. Evaluated on 60 queries (50 from a HuggingFace text-to-SQL dataset and 10 custom domain queries), the system achieves 90% correctness using Mistral across seven coordinated LLM calls showing that this approach can substantially increase the reliability of NL2SQL pipelines in high-stakes environments.

As automation reshapes work, employees increasingly interact with intelligent systems rather than perform core tasks directly. Drawing on Campion’s job design perspective and Affective Events Theory, this study examines the double-edged effects of human-machine interaction (HMI) on metro drivers’ safety performance. We propose that HMI enhances safety compliance and safety participation by reducing job tension. However, HMI may also undermine these safety outcomes by increasing work-related boredom. We further identify organizational readiness for change as a key boundary condition. Using three-wave, multi-source data from 454 metro drivers and 69 supervisors in China, we find that HMI improves safety performance through reduced job tension but undermines it through increased work-related boredom. In addition, organizational readiness for change strengthens the former pathway while weakening the latter. These findings extend HMI research by highlighting affective mechanisms, advance a job design perspective on automation-enabled work, and underscore the importance of organizational context.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being integrated into gastrointestinal and complex surgical care, yet its practical impact on nursing work remains insufficiently defined.This narrative review examines how nursing leadership can support the safe use of AI across perioperative pathways and how its effects can be evaluated through measurable nursing-sensitive outcomes.Literature was identified through PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science, with emphasis on peer-reviewed studies, systematic reviews, guidelines, consensus statements, and implementation frameworks relevant to gastrointestinal surgery, perioperative nursing, clinical decision support, and AI.The review focuses on preoperative assessment, intraoperative coordination, postoperative surveillance, and discharge planning in high-acuity surgical settings.Particular attention is given to workflow efficiency, response times, early recognition of complications, risk-stratified care, documentation quality, interdisciplinary communication, cognitive workload, and patient safety.The proposed framework is intended as a practical, non-validated structure for future evaluation rather than as an established measurement instrument.Its use will require prospective validation and adaptation to local staffing, digital infrastructure, resources, and clinical workflows.AI should therefore be judged not only by predictive performance, but by whether it helps nurses recognize risk earlier, communicate concerns clearly, and deliver safer perioperative care.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Burnout among healthcare professionals is an important occupational health concern that may negatively affect individual well-being, healthcare workforce sustainability, and quality of care. Anesthesiologists are particularly vulnerable to burnout due to high workload, clinical responsibility, time pressure, and irregular working schedules. However, the occupational mechanisms underlying burnout among anesthesiologists remain insufficiently understood. This study aimed to investigate the associations of job demands and job resources with burnout among Chinese anesthesiologists based on the Job Demands–Resources (JD–R) model. A multicenter cross-sectional survey was conducted among anesthesiologists from 72 hospitals across 22 provinces in China from June 16 to June 30, 2026. The ethics exemption was approved on June 11, 2026. Participants were recruited using a multicenter purposive sampling method and completed a general information questionnaire, a JD–R model-based questionnaire, and the Maslach Burnout Inventory–Human Services Survey (MBI-HSS). Burnout status was assessed according to established criteria. Differences in demographic and occupational characteristics between burnout and non-burnout groups were examined using chi-square tests. Spearman correlation analyses were performed to evaluate associations between job demands, job resources, and burnout dimensions. Hierarchical multivariable logistic regression models were constructed to identify factors independently associated with burnout. All statistical analyses were performed using R software and RStudio (version 2026.01.2 + 418). Among the 698 anesthesiologists included in the analysis, 324 (46.4%) met the criteria for burnout. Significant differences between burnout and non-burnout groups were observed in sex, age, educational level, marital status, professional title, work experience, weekly working hours, and number of night shifts. Higher job demands were positively correlated with emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and reduced personal accomplishment, whereas greater job resources showed negative correlations with all three burnout dimensions. In the fully adjusted model (Model 4), participants aged 31–40 years (vs. ≤ 30 years: OR = 9.677, 95% CI 2.287–40.940) and 41–50 years (OR = 8.305, 95% CI 1.705–40.463) had higher odds of burnout, whereas married participants (vs. unmarried: OR = 0.221, 95% CI 0.096–0.508) and those with more than 10 years of work experience (vs. < 5 years: OR = 0.178, 95% CI 0.050–0.638) had lower odds. At the sample mean of job resources, higher job demands were associated with higher odds of burnout (OR = 1.287, 95% CI 1.228–1.350); at the sample mean of job demands, higher job resources were associated with lower odds (OR = 0.850, 95% CI 0.808–0.893). Their interaction was statistically significant (OR = 1.009, 95% CI 1.003–1.016, P = 0.006). Burnout is relatively common among Chinese anesthesiologists and represents an important occupational health challenge. Consistent with the JD–R model, higher job demands were associated with increased likelihood of burnout, whereas greater job resources were associated with reduced likelihood after adjustment for demographic and occupational factors. These findings may inform future evaluations of organizational strategies that optimize workload and strengthen workplace resources.

Background: Traffic police personnel perform physically demanding duties involving prolonged standing, intermittent walking, repetitive weight-bearing, and exposure to variable road surfaces. These occupational conditions may contribute to foot discomfort, lower-limb fatigue, and musculoskeletal symptoms. Foot posture, anthropometric characteristics, standing duration, and occupational footwear are important factors to consider when evaluating foot health. Objective: This review examines the existing literature on occupational foot health, with particular emphasis on foot posture, prolonged standing, footwear comfort, body mass index (BMI), foot pain, and functional disability among traffic police personnel and other occupational groups with similar work demands. Review approach: A narrative review approach was used to organize relevant literature on foot posture assessment, occupational standing, footwear characteristics, and musculoskeletal health. Published clinical assessment studies and occupational health reviews were considered. The review emphasizes the relevance of these findings to traffic police personnel in Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh, India. Review findings: The literature indicates that prolonged standing is associated with several adverse health outcomes, including lower-limb discomfort and fatigue. Footwear characteristics, such as cushioning, sole hardness, fit, and insole design, may influence foot comfort and mechanical loading. Standardized tools, including the Foot Posture Index-6 (FPI-6), can support quantitative assessment of standing foot posture. However, static foot posture, pain intensity, and functional disability represent different outcomes and should be assessed separately. The available evidence does not establish that age, BMI, or standing duration necessarily causes a particular foot posture in traffic police personnel. Conclusion: Occupational foot health should be considered an important component of preventive health assessment among traffic police personnel. Future research in Bareilly should investigate foot posture, footwear comfort, standing duration, BMI, pain, and functional limitations using standardized assessment methods. Evidence from appropriately designed studies may inform occupational health screening and further evaluation of preventive strategies.

AI agents increasingly use files and software tools to produce professional deliverables. Such work draws on materials, decisions, and feedback accumulated across assignments. We introduce OfficeTown, a generative simulation framework for professional organizations in which tasks and their context arise from continuing organizational work. From a natural-language description of an organization's purpose and activities, OfficeTown initializes an organization whose members coordinate work, delegate bounded assignments to assistant agents, and review their deliverables. Artifacts, decisions, and unresolved matters persist and shape subsequent work, while responsibilities and permissions determine what each member can see and do. We curate work requests, their context, and review feedback into executable resources for evaluation and learning. We construct OfficeTown Bench with 406 tasks and 4,836 evaluation criteria from 23 simulated organizations across eight professional domains, incorporating domain-expert feedback. Frontier-model evaluations reveal substantial remaining headroom. Supervised fine-tuning and on-policy distillation on OfficeTown data substantially improve Qwen3.5-9B on external professional-work benchmarks, including GDPval. Supplementary evaluations show that the principal--assistant harness achieves higher scores than the single- and multi-agent baselines tested. These results highlight the value of organizational simulation in generating work-grounded data and environments for the continued development of generalist agents.

Despite the rise of artificial intelligence, human intuition endures as both a foundation for education and also (for now) a primarily human experience. We re-examine a formula for the sum of squares that is sometimes set aside because of possible numerical issues. The formula can be used to create square doughnuts, a delicious regional favorite. The variance becomes the dough, and we can examine the variance by either comparing doughnuts or by making different sizes of doughnuts with the same amount of dough. In doing so, we provide a new visualization of a cornerstone formula, understandable by students at almost any level. We further provide insight into related topics such as the coefficient of variation as well as a visualization of when numerical issues are likely to be problematic. We also provide a new vocabulary for understanding the variance formula, with `dough' and `hole' taking the place of less edible concepts from the typical recipe.

When an aircraft accident or another serious emergency occurs at an airport, an independent ground handling provider may work under several emergency arrangements at once: the aerodrome emergency plan, the emergency response plans of the airlines it serves, its own plan and the emergency provisions of occupational health and safety law. This paper examines how public regulatory and guidance documents position the provider within these nested arrangements. A document analysis of 21 international, European, national and industry sources, recorded with their legal status and access level, was combined with research on interorganisational coordination in emergencies. Each document was coded for nine emergency functions, distinguishing explicit, implicit, not stated and not assessable provisions; only the third category was treated as evidence of absence. The European acceptable means of compliance and guidance material for ground handling organisations, issued in 2025, now address the provider directly: they require corporate and station level emergency response plans, coordination with aerodrome and aircraft operators, support for or substitution of the aircraft operator's plan, contact arrangements, training and testing. Precedence of aerodrome procedures is stated for listed operational aspects. In the documents reviewed in full, no provision was found on how a provider that serves several airlines should allocate staff and equipment committed to more than one plan, and functions such as passenger information, family assistance and dangerous goods information remain assigned to the airline without provisions on their performance through an agent. The paper argues that the main unresolved problem is the multiple commitment of the same resources, and that questions of authority must be separated into procedure, command, employer duty, delegated tasks and resource allocation. Implications for handling agreements, aerodrome plans and multiairline exercises are discussed

Nigeria’ s energy sector is marred by structural inefficiencies, unreliable grid infrastructure, and an overdependence on fossil fuels, resulting in inadequate electricity access and persistent blackouts. Despite possessing vast renewable energy resources—particularly solar and wind—the country continues to underutilize them due to technical, financial, and regulatory barriers. This study examines the transformative potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in addressing these challenges and optimizing renewable energy generation, distribution, and management. Employing a qualitative secondary research methodology, the study analyzes peerreviewed literature, national policy documents, and global case studies to evaluate the applicability of AI technologies such as machine learning, neural networks, and predictive analytics within the Nigerian context. Case studies of solar farms, wind energy forecasting, smart grid operations, and urban load management illustrate how AI can enhance forecasting accuracy, improve grid reliability, reduce operational costs, and support decentralized energy access in rural areas. However, the adoption of AI faces significant hurdles, including high implementation costs, limited technical expertise, and a lack of robust data infrastructure. To overcome these barriers, the study recommends strategic public-private partnerships, targeted capacity-building programs, supportive data policy frameworks, and pilot initiatives to demonstrate feasibility. The integration of AI into Nigeria’ s renewable energy systems offers a promising pathway toward achieving national energy security, sustainability, and socioeconomic development.

Heart failure and cardiovascular diseases are two severe medical problem which needs immediate preventive mea sures and early recognition of risk factors. Cardiovascular Car diovascular cardiovascular cardiovascular cardiovascular cardio vascular risk. But, many of the existing prediction systems focus more on developing a risk stratification than providing patient specific recommendations tailored to their clinical conditions. In this paper, we propose an Enhanced Machine Learning System for heart failure as well as Personalised Health Recom mendation Engine. To discover an effective prediction model, the proposed system collects demographic, clinical and lifestyle related data, preprocess it, select the features and evaluates various machine learning algorithms. It includes a risk category, prediction probability, confidence data along with Heart Health Score in the output of the prediction. The main contribution of the proposed system is the Person alised Recommendation Engine which takes machine learning predictions and circadian rhythm parameters (blood pressure, cholesterol, BMI, diabetes status, smoking habits) with phys ical activity, sleep duration stress level and dietary habits as individual parameters. Instead of issuing the same prevention recommendations to every user in a specific risk group, it produces individualized preventive recommendations based on each user's health profile. Explainable Artificial Intelligence methods can be adopted to ascertain the factors that impact the prediction. All these services are brought together under one interac tive web-based system through the proposed framework. It is interactive, user-centric, user-centric, user-centric, user-centric, user-centric, and user-centric.

Can large language model (LLM) agents deliver expert-level operations research (OR) solutions directly from original client materials, without prior expert reformulation? Existing OR benchmarks typically begin with self-contained descriptions or predefined optimization tasks, underrepresenting the translation of original business materials into professionally validated solutions. We introduce OR-License, an end-to-end benchmark of 31 instances across 10 industrial scenarios from paid OR engagements totaling USD 3.68 million. It preserves original requirements, input data, deliverable formats, and information boundaries after de-identification. To study information acquisition, we introduce ORSim, a controlled client simulator that discloses business facts without supplying OR expertise. Hidden evaluation checks feasibility and compares objective quality against original expert solutions accepted by clients before benchmark construction. Deployment-Adjusted Quality (DAQ) averages expert-relative quality across instances, assigning zero to infeasible deliveries. Across 11 frontier LLMs using coding-agent harnesses, several exceed the expert reference in conditional objective quality, but none matches its DAQ; the strongest primary Claude Code configuration achieves 88.39% strict feasibility and a DAQ of 0.87 against the expert reference of 1. Client information acquisition extends beyond clarification into solution development and validation, with some later stages showing higher confirmed issue-resolution proportions. Trajectory analysis identifies formulation and implementation failures, while task-equalized research-chain completion rates range from 24% to 45% across models on evaluable tasks. These findings motivate sustained information-gap resolution, faithful problem formulation, and evidence-linked self-improvement for reliable long-horizon agents.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: In-Context Learning (ICL) enables pretrained LLMs to adapt to downstream tasks from a small set of input-output demonstrations, without parameter updates. Yet existing theory primarily explains ICL as identifying a latent task already represented in pretraining, leaving unclear whether ICL can succeed when either the instruction or the target task falls outside the pretraining support. We develop a theoretical framework under mild assumptions that separates these two forms of distribution shift. For target tasks represented in pretraining, we show that demonstrations can identify the task and reduce sensitivity to pretrain-supported prompt templates as their number increases. For an unsupported instruction, we show that under a fixed model-induced reference extension, demonstration evidence can dominate an $N$-independent instruction shift while preserving the exponential identification rate. We then use the same ICL framework as an interpretive lens for long-horizon target tasks that are not represented in pretraining but admit a plan that decomposes them into pretraining-supported subtasks. Applying the supported-task analysis step by step yields a standard accumulated-error bound and clarifies how invoking familiar subtasks along an intermediate-state trajectory can avoid directly selecting the unsupported complete task. Together, our results characterize when demonstrations, instructions, and task decomposition can support ICL beyond the corresponding pretraining supports.

Chain-of-Thought (CoT) monitoring offers actionable evidence for oversight AI systems, with the potential to enable early detection and intervention. However, existing approaches are focused on specific tasks, whereas the regulation of AI, particularly reasoning models, requires monitoring a broader range of tasks. We introduce Factor for CoT monitoring, a strategy that supports customizing monitoring requirements in the prompt, which enables a single monitor to cover different tasks by relying on different factors. Furthermore, we introduce two types of factors, fine-grained and coarse-grained (e.g., monitoring whether a specific email address has been leaked versus monitoring privacy leakage), to accommodate diverse user monitoring needs. Based on this, we develop a CoT monitor named OwlSight that relies solely on factor to monitor behaviors related to multiple dimensions, including capability, safety, and trustworthiness. Experiments across 15,971 reasoning trajectories show that OwlSight surpasses general-purpose LLMs by 1.32-30.57 and 11.71-27.81 points at fine and coarse granularity, respectively, and achieves state-of-the-art results on OpenAI's CoT monitorability benchmark. It also generalizes to unseen models' CoTs and remains robust to Factor rephrasings, CoT compression, and obfuscation, offering a promising paradigm for CoT monitoring that can contribute to the oversight of frontier AI.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Serving DNN inference is costly, yet a single task seldom saturates both the compute units and the memory bandwidth of a GPU. GPU sharing raises utilization by co-locating several tasks on one GPU, at the cost of interference among them. Existing systems estimate this interference with binary compute-memory rules, standalone scaling curves, or model-level predictors. However, these estimates rest on a limited understanding of interference. They leave the software and hardware properties of co-located operators largely unexplored and give no slowdown prediction that is both interpretable and accurate. We conduct an operator-level study of interference under SM partitioning and use hardware counters to trace it to contention on the shared memory path, where the slowdown depends jointly on both co-located operators. Based on these findings, we propose PairSight, a hardware-aware interference predictor that learns how the hardware behaviors of co-located tasks interact and predicts the latency of each task before co-location. On six DNN models including LLMs, PairSight predicts latency under sharing with 4.3% mean error, against 19.0% for a compute-memory intensity rule, and adapts to unseen models and inputs with a few samples.

Multi-objective optimization models are often deployed in settings where decision makers (DMs) must balance some conflicting criteria. In practice, however, stakeholders must translate their qualitative preferences between different criteria into numerical weights, priorities, or reference points required by optimization methods, which can be difficult to specify and interpret. This paper proposes \emph{ParetoChat}, an LLM (large language model)-based expert-agent interface for interactive multi-objective optimization. The agent translates natural-language user input into structured scalarization parameters, invokes an optimization system, presents candidate solutions, and iteratively elicits feedback. We describe a multi-agent architecture that separates input processing, multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) expertise, solution presentation, and feedback processing. We then present a simulation study using an LLM-based DM agent and benchmark ParetoChat against interactive methods implemented in DESDEO, including reference-point and NIMBUS methods. The computational experiments on multi-objective binary knapsack and set-partitioning instances show that ParetoChat can guide the search efficiently toward solutions that match the DM's preferences. An application to historical courier-order assignment instances illustrates how users can explore objective extremes and intermediate trade-offs through natural-language requests. The results indicate that LLM agents may provide a practical interaction layer between business stakeholders and optimization tools.

Prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) show that pretraining on large populations of synthetic tasks can enable generalization to unseen datasets with little or no downstream fine-tuning. This paradigm is effective for transformer-based tabular and relational foundation models such as RDB-PFN, but remains largely unexplored for graph-based relational models built on message passing. We pretrain the graph-based relational foundation model Griffin on large collections of synthetic relational databases and ask whether curriculum learning, which benefits transformer-based relational learners, also improves message-passing representations. Rather than fine-tune on downstream tasks, we use the pretrained encoder as a general-purpose relational representation learner and pass its latent representations to a frozen in-context predictor (\ticl{}); no component is trained on the target task. On 16 real-world relational classification tasks, evaluated over five seeds against raw-feature and untrained-encoder baselines, a purely synthetic curriculum that begins with schema-guided data and continues with schema-agnostic data gives the strongest frozen in-context performance\rev{, outperforming real-data-only pretraining and every unordered single-stage mixture of the corpora; when appended after real-data pretraining, it yields the best encoders overall}. These results provide initial evidence that PFN-style synthetic pretraining transfers to graph-based relational foundation models.

This chapter analyzes an academic strategy based on a prompting guide for co-creating educational content with AI in distance learning undergraduate programs at a Peruvian university. Using a descriptive-applied approach, the study combines the evaluation of instructional products and the perceptions of content teachers to assess the quality of the content generated, as well as the strategy itself. The results show that the content is of very good quality, highlighting pedagogical mediation, institutional intentionality, and the active role of the teacher as central factors for the responsible integration of artificial intelligence. The chapter provides conceptual and practical guidance for the development of educational resources mediated by artificial intelligence in distance education contexts.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can now perceive, describe, and reason about images and audio, yet time series understanding remains underestimated: most work uses LLMs as forecasters and classifiers, reasoning studies are few and narrow, and no suite trains and evaluates the full range of capabilities. In this paper, we build the first such suite, with 337K training and 44K evaluation samples across three progressive capabilities, Perceive, Solve, and Reason, and use it to ask how time series should enter an LLM that must master all three, and in what order. We find that a dedicated encoder is essential: with one, a 4B model surpasses GPT-4o on every perception attribute we test, whereas textualizing the series costs 8--10 points in reasoning accuracy. The capabilities then build on one another: learning them in order beats mixing the same data and rivals reasoning-only training with over three times the reasoning data, but only when an encoder is used. Analyses further reveal that capabilities are transferred through distinct network depths rather than simply stacked, and that a stage converged on its own benchmark is not necessarily ready for the next. Distilled into a simple recipe, these findings yield 4B TS-LLMs that, without any target-domain data, outperform four recent 7B TS-LLMs on seven of eight out-of-domain metrics, by up to 11 points. We therefore advocate treating time series as a first-class modality for LLMs, read through dedicated encoders and taught to perceive before they reason.

Artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) is increasingly embedded in short-video platforms, where algorithmic recommendation systems expose users to high volumes of rapidly produced synthetic media. Although prior research has examined generative AI from the perspectives of creativity, productivity, and technology adoption, less is known about how ordinary users evaluate repeated exposure to AI-generated short videos. This study develops and tests an appraisal-based model of AI content fatigue, distinguishing perceived AIGC saturation from users' appraisals of low-quality prevalence, narrative homogenization, and content overload. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among Chinese short-video users in May 2026. After excluding invalid responses, 513 valid questionnaires were analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling. The adjusted structural model showed acceptable fit to the data, χ²(1321) = 1991.541, χ²/df = 1.508, CFI = .946, TLI = .929, IFI = .947, and RMSEA = .031. Perceived AIGC saturation was positively associated with perceived low-quality prevalence, perceived narrative homogenization, and perceived content overload. Perceived low-quality prevalence had the largest estimated coefficient, followed by perceived content overload, whereas perceived narrative homogenization was not supported under bootstrap inference. AI content fatigue was negatively associated with satisfaction and continued viewing intention. Bootstrap analyses indicated selected path-specific indirect associations from perceived AIGC saturation to AI content fatigue, satisfaction, and continued viewing intention. Indirect pathways through perceived low-quality prevalence and perceived content overload were supported, whereas those through perceived narrative homogenization were not. The findings indicate that fatigue in AIGC-rich short-video environments is not simply a response to AI-generated content itself. It is more closely related to users' appraisals of content quality, repetitiveness, and cognitive burden. The study contributes to social media fatigue research by conceptualizing AI content fatigue as a content-specific evaluative state and offers implications for platform governance, AIGC labeling, recommendation diversity, and quality-sensitive moderation.

Introduction Despite the rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in sports broadcasting, empirical evidence validating the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and experiential outcomes in this specific context remains limited. This study aims to address this gap by investigating the statistical relationships among core TAM constructs, usage attitude, behavioral intention, and perceived viewing-experience enhancement within AI-based sports broadcasting services. Methods Based on the theoretical framework of TAM, this study collected valid data from 630 Chinese respondents. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was employed to quantitatively test the hypothesized research model and examine the interrelationships between the proposed variables. Results The empirical results demonstrate that perceived ease of use positively predicts perceived usefulness, and both perceived ease of use and perceived usefulness exert significant positive effects on users' usage attitude. Furthermore, usage attitude is positively associated with behavioral intention and perceived viewing-experience enhancement. Notably, usage attitude plays a full mediating role in the relationships between the two perceptual antecedents (perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness) and the two outcome variables (behavioral intention, viewing-experience enhancement). Discussion This research contributes context-specific empirical validation to the TAM framework in the emerging domain of AI-driven sports broadcasting. It extends existing TAM literature by integrating individual-level experiential outcomes alongside traditional behavioral intention indicators in sports media consumption. Practically, the findings provide actionable insights for optimizing user experience and improving service design for AI sports broadcasting platforms.

This study investigates the evolution of perception in architectural drawing, tracing the shift from hand-drawn sketches to computer-assisted techniques and immersive virtual reality. Through a comprehensive theoretical review and comparative analysis, it explores how these tools reshape spatial representation and enhance creative expression, with a particular focus on the pedagogical implications for drawing instruction in universities. The research explores the evolution of our understanding of perceptual processes over time, focusing on descriptive geometry's role in conceptualizing and communicating complex spatial forms. Findings point to a balanced synergy, advocating a hybrid approach that integrates the intuitive creativity of hand-drawn sketches with the technical precision of digital tools. Informed by classroom experiences, this proposed methodology empowers architectural students to navigate technological advancements while preserving the cognitive engagement and artistic intuition essential to drawing. The study contributes significantly to spatial design knowledge, providing actionable insights for architects, educators, and researchers on nurturing creativity through integrated representational practices that bridge historical techniques with contemporary technologies in the teaching/learning environment

Natural Language Processing (NLP) is a branch of artificial intelligence that is widely used to analyze whether a sentence contains positive, negative, or neutral sentiment, particularly in the context of expressing opinions in the online environment. This study compares several models to identify the most optimal one, namely Naïve Bayes, Support Vector Machine (SVM), XGBoost, and IndoBERT. The dataset used in this research was obtained from Kaggle and consists of 5,644 data points in the neutral class, 2,934 data points in the positive class, and 2,606 data points in the negative class. Prior to model implementation, the dataset underwent a preprocessing stage that included case folding, cleansing, tokenization, stemming, and stopword removal. Subsequently, the data were trained using the four aforementioned methods. The results indicate that Naïve Bayes achieved an accuracy of 75%, SVM reached 79%, XGBoost obtained 76%, while IndoBERT achieved the highest accuracy at 85%. Therefore, it can be concluded that, using this dataset, IndoBERT performed sentiment classification very effectively.

Introduction: Large language models (LLMs) can pass the US medical licensing exam and outperform residents on the family medicine in-training exam. The diagnostic performance of LLMs when applied to more complex medical cases, however, remains unknown.Methods: We evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of Claude (Anthropic), an LLM, on 20 case challenges published in The New England Journal of Medicine (NEJM). For each case, we presented Claude 3.5 Sonnet with multimodal input, including the text and all corresponding images from the cases. Claude was instructed to give an answer among multiple choices. We compared Claude’s diagnostic accuracy to human respondents on the NEJM website.Results: Claude 3.5 Sonnet diagnosed cases correctly about half the time, and at a significantly higher rate than NEJM readers (beta-binomial odds ratio 2.79; 95% CI [profile-likelihood] 1.09–7.01; P = 0.031). Claude was highly self-consistent in repeated exposure to questions, with perfect accuracy (100%) in nine cases and no accuracy (0%) in 10 cases, with one case at 90% accuracy. Human accuracy ranged from 9%–63% across cases. Claude’s performance was better on easier cases (ie, those with human accuracy >25%).Conclusions: Claude 3.5 Sonnet demonstrated significantly higher diagnostic accuracy compared to medical journal readers, though with notable variability in performance. Further research comparing consistency and reliability of artificially intelligent diagnostic capabilities to that of licensed physicians is needed.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Background Large language model (LLM) chatbots are increasingly used by the public to obtain health information, but the safety and quality of their responses to questions about osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures (OVCFs) remain unclear. Objective To compare the safety and patient-facing response quality of four publicly accessible LLM chatbots when responding to standardized questions about osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures. Methods In this cross-sectional paired evaluation, 36 standardized OVCF-related patient-facing questions were submitted to each of four publicly accessible LLM chatbot interfaces—ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Doubao—in an initial response-generation round on June 20, 2026, from Jiangsu, China. Queries were conducted in English in independent single-turn sessions under matched conditions, yielding 144 responses for the primary between-chatbot analysis. A second independent generation round using the same 36 questions and matched query procedures was conducted 7 days later (June 27, 2026), yielding an additional 144 responses for within-model stability analysis. The questions covered symptoms and warning signs, diagnosis and imaging, conservative management, medication safety, rehabilitation, vertebral augmentation, fracture prevention, and special clinical scenarios. Five clinical raters, blinded to chatbot identity and generation round, independently evaluated safety, factual accuracy, empathic communication, treatment-related information quality using DISCERN, patient-information quality using EQIP, transparency using the JAMA benchmark criteria, and overall quality using the Global Quality Score. Readability was assessed automatically using six established indices. Between-chatbot comparisons and test–retest stability analyses used paired methods appropriate for the outcome type. Results Inter-rater agreement was high, with a Fleiss’ kappa of 0.818 for safety and ICC(2,1) values of 0.816 for accuracy, 0.820 for empathy, 0.820 for DISCERN, 0.820 for EQIP, 0.821 for JAMA, and 0.818 for GQS. Potentially unsafe responses were identified for every chatbot: 3 of 36 ChatGPT responses (8.3%), 5 of 36 DeepSeek responses (13.9%), 6 of 36 Gemini responses (16.7%), and 7 of 36 Doubao responses (19.4%). The overall paired difference in safety was not statistically significant (Cochran's Q = 3.621, df = 3, P = 0.305). Factual accuracy differed significantly but only modestly among chatbots ( P = 0.009; Kendall's W = 0.108). Empathy showed substantially greater variation ( P < 0.001; W = 0.817), with higher scores for ChatGPT and Gemini than for DeepSeek and Doubao. DISCERN, EQIP, JAMA benchmark, and GQS scores also differed significantly among chatbots (all P < 0.001). Doubao produced responses with the greatest estimated textual complexity. Across the two generation rounds, safety agreement ranged from 88.9% to 97.2% (Gwet's AC1, 0.838–0.966), and median ICC(2,1) values across the 12 non-safety outcomes ranged from 0.781 to 0.904. Conclusions In this time-stamped, single-location, two-round evaluation, all four chatbot interfaces produced some responses classified as potentially unsafe despite generally high clinician-rated factual accuracy. Differences were greater in empathy, information quality, transparency, overall quality, and readability than in factual accuracy. The observed within-model stability was generally good but did not eliminate variability across generations. These findings are specific to the evaluated access location, language, single-turn conditions, and generation dates and should not be assumed to represent stable performance across settings or future model updates. LLM-generated OVCF information should not be used as a standalone patient education resource; any potential use should involve clinician oversight, safety safeguards, and further validation.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: We introduce the perpetual openness invariant: a mechanical mechanism that guarantees an LLM-based reasoning loop never halts at a fixed point. Crystallization negates itself via $D(-\iota -w.\text{presence})$ re-entry; the operator re-enters genesis with dimension = 1, tension = 2.0, cavity deepened, history accumulated, and phase = growth; the loop runs its whole extrinsic budget-compute, never an intrinsic fixed point. Halt only when even the reset fails (substrate_unrecoverable: reality itself died under the loop—a crash, not a closure). We verify the invariant on a self-improving kernel (BENBEN/EGO1) whose two-shot loop (Paryudasa Prasajya) operates on real external friction: test failures measured in subprocesses, diffs applied via git apply, and accept/discard decisions that determine whether the operator grows or is purged. Empirical results on 34 end-to-end tests (33 pass, 1 skip for live FCC endpoint) confirm the invariant holds across diverse mutation classes.

Abstract High solar activity can significantly impact Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) signals, leading to loss-of-lock (LoL) events in satellite-based receivers. A LoL occurs when a GNSS receiver can no longer maintain signal tracking from a satellite, resulting in degraded positioning accuracy. Here, we analyze LoL occurrence using observations from the European Space Agency Swarm satellite mission spanning 2014 to 2025. While LoL events generally correlate with solar activity, reflecting increased intensity of processes driving ionospheric irregularities during active periods, since 2023 a subset of events over Europe and western Asia has been identified that cannot be explained by ionospheric irregularities. These unexplained events coincide spatially and temporally with regions and periods where independent reports document widespread GNSS interference linked to military operations. This study highlights the capability of scientific satellite constellations to detect and characterize GNSS interference, with benefits for space weather research, technological resilience, and situational awareness in conflict regions.

Chinese Herbal Medicine (CHM) has been widely used for centuries and remains an important component of healthcare systems worldwide.The increasing integration of Chinese herbal medicine into modern medicine has intensified interest in understanding its pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic characteristics and their contributions to therapeutic efficacy.This review aims to summarize current knowledge regarding the pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, mechanisms of action, therapeutic applications, and safety considerations of Chinese Herbal Medicine.A comprehensive literature review was conducted using peer-reviewed articles retrieved from major scientific databases, including Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar.Relevant studies addressing absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, pharmacological mechanisms, herb-drug interactions, and advanced analytical approaches were evaluated and organized into thematic categories.Evidence indicates that Chinese Herbal Medicine exerts therapeutic effects through complex multi-component and multi-target interactions.Pharmacokinetic processes influence the bioavailability and disposition of herbal constituents, whereas pharmacodynamic mechanisms involve modulation of receptors, enzymes, signaling pathways, and gene expression.Emerging approaches such as network pharmacology, chinmedomics, and pharmacometabolomics have improved the understanding of the molecular basis of Chinese Herbal Medicine efficacy.However, challenges related to standardization, quality control, and herb-drug interactions remain significant.Integration of pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic evidence provides a scientific foundation for understanding the efficacy and safety of Chinese Herbal Medicine.Future advances in systems biology, artificial intelligence, and precision medicine may facilitate the development of more effective and personalized herbal therapies.

This article examines current aspects of multiple sclerosis as a chronic demyelinating disease of the central nervous system associated with diverse neurological impairments that may lead to persistent disability and a reduced quality of life. Current approaches to early diagnosis are analyzed, including magnetic resonance imaging, clinical assessment, and the McDonald diagnostic criteria, together with the classification of demyelinating diseases according to the International Classification of Diseases, 11th Revision. Data on the prevalence of multiple sclerosis worldwide and in Ukraine, its main clinical manifestations, risk factors, immunopathogenetic mechanisms, and current approaches to pharmacotherapy are summarized. Particular attention is paid to the importance of timely medical consultation, interdisciplinary collaboration among healthcare professionals, physical therapy, and occupational therapy in restoring and maintaining patients’ functional abilities. The prospects for using digital technologies and artificial intelligence to monitor patients’ condition and improve rehabilitation interventions are considered. The importance of a comprehensive approach to the care of people with multiple sclerosis is emphasized, with a focus on maintaining functional independence, improving quality of life, and reducing the risk of disability progression.

Oral drug delivery remains the most widely preferred route of drug administration owing to its convenience, patient compliance, cost-effectiveness, and suitability for long-term therapy.However, the oral delivery of many therapeutic agents is significantly limited by poor aqueous solubility, low intestinal permeability, gastrointestinal degradation, extensive first-pass metabolism, and efflux transporter activity, resulting in inadequate bioavailability and inconsistent therapeutic outcomes.Polymeric nanospheres have emerged as a promising nanotechnology-based platform capable of overcoming these physiological and biopharmaceutical barriers through enhanced drug protection, controlled release, improved mucosal interaction, and targeted intestinal absorption.The selection of appropriate biodegradable polymers, together with advances in formulation technologies such as nanoprecipitation, solvent evaporation, microfluidics, and continuous manufacturing, has considerably improved the physicochemical properties and therapeutic performance of oral nanosphere formulations.Furthermore, recent developments in surface engineering, stimuli-responsive polymers, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted formulation design, machine learning (ML), and Quality by Design (QbD) have accelerated the optimization and translation of polymeric nanospheres from laboratory research toward industrial manufacturing.This review comprehensively summarizes the fundamental principles, classification, formulation strategies, characterization techniques, drug release mechanisms, surface functionalization approaches, and smart polymeric nanosphere systems developed for oral drug delivery.In addition, recent therapeutic applications in cancer, diabetes, infectious diseases, inflammatory disorders, neurological diseases, and biological therapeutics are critically discussed.The review also highlights current translational challenges, regulatory considerations, clinical perspectives, and future research directions with particular emphasis on intelligent nanomedicine, precision drug delivery, and sustainable pharmaceutical manufacturing.Overall, polymeric nanospheres represent a versatile and rapidly evolving oral drug delivery platform with significant potential to improve drug bioavailability, therapeutic efficacy, and patient outcomes while facilitating the development of next-generation oral nanomedicines.

Introduction: Cardiac arrest is a common cause of morbidity and mortality in hospitalized patients, and is a critical event that hospital-based physicians must be prepared to manage. While cardiac arrest care follows established algorithms, management of patients after return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) is more dynamic and nuanced. Resident physicians therefore need structured training to provide high-quality post-ROSC care. Methods: We developed a 90-minute simulation session on postarrest care for internal medicine interns. The session included 2 simulation cases: one involving a patient with ventricular tachycardia arrest in the intensive care unit, and another featuring a patient with pulseless electrical activity arrest in an acute care setting. Interns alternated between roles as participants and observers to both practice and analyze communication and clinical skills. Between simulation cases, a brief teaching talk was delivered to review a framework for post-ROSC care. The curriculum was evaluated using pre- and postsession questionnaires to evaluate changes in knowledge and confidence. Results: Thirty-four learners participated in our curriculum over 2 academic years.
